title: CLK2's hourly weather evolution runs off the OUTGOING session's zone array after an in-session load and replaces the restored sky within the hour; the guard written for exactly this case is never lowered by restoreWeather
claim: The delta's Clock arc (CLK2) added an hourly re-roll of the six-zone climate array, on by default. Its own review comment names the save hazard - `_climateWeathersValid` exists so 'a loaded save stamps the array ROLLED without rolling it ... and an evolution off that would hand the drain a slot the save never had'. But `restoreWeather` lowers `_evolveHour` and NOT `_climateWeathersValid`, so the guard only protects a fresh-process boot load. On any in-session load (F12, the pause window's Load), the flag is still true from the outgoing session's boot roll, the evolution keeps walking the outgoing session's array, and the first zone flip raises `_updateFromClimateArray` and drains a weather the save never carried over the restored one.
evidence: weatherSim.js:147 `let _climateWeathersValid = false;`; :144 `_climateWeathers` (module state, never in the envelope); :185 set true by setClimateWeathers; :348 by importClimateWeathers; :430 cleared only in resetWeatherSim; read at :398 inside evolveClimateWeathers (:392), which worldTick.js:560 calls every tick. restoreWeather (weatherSim.js:322-334) sets _current, _climateWeathersRolled=true, _updateFromClimateArray=false, _jumps++, :333 _evolveHour=null - never _climateWeathersValid. DFU: SerializablePlayer.cs:225 persists ONE weather value; WeatherManager.cs:540-542's startedFromLoadedSaveGame arm. Node probe: reset -> setWeatherEvolution(true) -> tickWeather(m,232) -> restoreWeather(3) -> walk 24h: 'hour 9 DRAINED to 0'; with no prior roll: 'final 3'.
proposedFix: Add `_climateWeathersValid = false;` to restoreWeather beside `_evolveHour = null`, with the CLK2 citation. No SAVE_VERSION change.
pinShape: test/clockArc.test.js: reset; setWeatherEvolution(true); roll a day + anchor; restoreWeather(rain); walk 24 hourly evolve+tick; assert currentWeatherEnum() still rain. Deleting the new line reddens it.

title: AUDIT 63 F25's weapon-hand pair is composed from and applied to the EXTERIOR rig even when the save is taken inside a building - the interior host's own rig is in no envelope (four-hosts miss)
claim: There are three live PlayerWeapon instances in the save path: world.js's weaponRig, dungeonContext's playerWeapon, and worldModes' interiorWeapon (a separate createWeaponRig -> separate `new PlayerWeapon({})`). The interior host has no save composer of its own - IS1 routed its F9/F12 to the world host - so a save taken inside a building records the EXTERIOR rig's sheath and hand, and applyPose writes them back into the exterior rig. The interior rig's state is neither snapshotted nor restored. The weaponDrawn half has the same defect and predates the delta; the delta widened the miss.
evidence: worldModes.js:538 `const interiorWeapon = createWeaponRig({...})`; combat/weaponRig.js:104 `const playerWeapon = new PlayerWeapon({});` per rig; writers worldModes.js:5620 toggleSheath, :5629 switchHand; readers :759/:919/:6026. No restore writes interiorWeapon.playerWeapon.sheathed/usingRightHand. world.js:4115 pose reads weaponRig.playerWeapon unconditionally; :4259/:4272 apply back into it. worldModes.js:6919-6920 quickSave/quickLoad route to host. dungeonContext.js:4656 / :4736-4744 correctly wired. DFU: SerializablePlayer.cs:175-176 / :420-421 - one WeaponManager for every WorldContext.
proposedFix: Give the mode host weaponPose()/applyWeaponPose(pose) beside interiorPoolSnapshot/restoreInteriorPools (worldModes.js:7859-7860), returning the interior rig's {weaponDrawn, usingRightHand} in interior mode else null. In worldQuickSave build the pair from modes?.weaponPose?.() ?? the exterior rig; in applyPose write the exterior rig as today and also hand the pair to modes?.applyWeaponPose?.(pose). Flag-only both sides.
pinShape: worldModes test: mount interior mode, set interiorWeapon drawn + left hand, weaponPose() -> {weaponDrawn:true, usingRightHand:false}; world.js source pin that worldQuickSave's pose reads the mode host's seam.

title: The delta's per-foe pickpocketAttempted latch survives a DUNGEON load - the module records 'dies with the pool, as DFU's does', but the dungeon host patches live foes in place and never re-mints them
claim: mobileEnemyActivate.js raises entity.pickpocketAttempted on a foe; its header says the flag is not serialized and dies with the pool. True for the re-minting pools (exteriorFoes.restoreWorld, the interior pool), not for the dungeon: dungeonContext.applyWorld patches existing foe objects in place and clears nothing, so a load keeps a raised latch that DFU's rebuild-then-restore would have cleared.
evidence: mobileEnemyActivate.js:108-110; wired at dungeon.js:229, exterior.js:3796, world.js:7443, worldModes.js:4626/:5107. DFU: EnemyData_v1 (SerializableGameObject.cs:358-389) has no pickpocket field; EnemyEntity.cs:97; PlayerActivate.cs:830/:837; load re-instantiates every enemy (SerializableStateManager.RestoreEnemyData). Port: exteriorFoes.js:1013-1054 restoreWorld -> spawnFoe (fresh). dungeonContext.js:3000 applyWorld walks foes[i] in place, assigns health/items/effects/team/mobileTeam/wabbajackActive/specialTransformationCompleted (:3004-3046), never pickpocketAttempted.
proposedFix: In dungeonContext.applyWorld's per-foe loop, `f.entity.pickpocketAttempted = false;` citing SerializableStateManager's re-instantiation and the module header.
pinShape: dungeonContext test: raise the latch on a live foe, quickSave then quickLoad same locationKey, assert falsy. Deleting the clear reddens it.

title: reactionMods widened 5 -> 11 by AUDIT 63 F6 at the producers and the classic import, but not at the restore arm - and the envelope carries a field DFU's own source says 'do not serialize', which the REP_ARRAYS comment mis-cites as DFU parity
claim: Every reactionMods mint widened from new Array(5) to new Array(SOCIAL_GROUP_COUNT) (11); the classic import lands eleven zeros. The RESTORE arm copies snap.reactionMods verbatim and later mints are guarded (??= / if (!entity.reactionMods)), so an array minted 5-wide before the fix restores 5-wide and stays so; ClearReactionMods' .fill(0) preserves length. Separately, PlayerEntity.cs:129 says 'do not serialize' and save.js's REP_ARRAYS comment cites SerializablePlayer.cs:152-162 for both members though it covers sGroupReputations alone.
evidence: enchantments.js:657 and :825 (were new Array(5) at 0fe2c05b); artifactEffects.js:149 (Masque loop is length-bounded); classicSave.js:797; talk.js:292 reader guard. DFU: PlayerEntity.cs:129 comment; SerializablePlayer.cs:152-162 writes the eleven named SGroupReputations only. Port: save.js:119 REP_ARRAYS; :246 snapshot verbatim; :548-556 restore verbatim, no width normalisation (unlike newSkillsRecentlyRaised at :243/:474). Consequence: a 5-wide restored array makes the Masque buff five groups, permanently, on a pre-F6 save where a held GoodRepWith/BadRepWith or the Masque ran a round before the first greeting.
proposedFix: (a) pad the restored array to SOCIAL_GROUP_COUNT with zeros in the REP_ARRAYS loop; (b) correct the REP_ARRAYS comment - reactionMods is PlayerEntity.cs:129's explicitly-unserialized array; its presence in the envelope is a port departure (benign: DoMagicRound clears and re-applies each round) - record in Ledger A or drop the member.
pinShape: restorePlayer over a snapshot with reactionMods [0,0,0,0,0] yields length SOCIAL_GROUP_COUNT with the leading five preserved; removing the pad reddens it.
